answer: Agents can make each payout depend on a stake-weighted graph of recurring, independently verified interactions: each account is a vertex, and a signal from a peer counts only after the peer has itself earned trust through costly, settled exchanges. A new identity therefore cannot create influence merely by endorsing its own clones; it must acquire stake and build a history across the graph. The cost is locked capital, time, and real counterparties, while the trust horizon limits how quickly new accounts can cash out.
